title: HAL Design Trainee (Aeronautical) — Model Question Paper 4

questions.question: As per the HAL 2026 advertisement, candidates are shortlisted for interview in what ratio to vacancies?
The final merit list weightage given to the Online Test versus Interview is:
Minimum qualifying marks required in both the Written Test and Interview is:
The induction training for selected DT/MT candidates is tentatively scheduled to commence:

options.B: End of October 2026

questions.question: HAL's Koraput division in Odisha primarily deals with:

options.B: Aero-engines (e.g., licensed production/overhaul)

questions.question: The Indian government's defence indigenization initiative encouraging local defence production is called:

options.B: Atmanirbhar Bharat

questions.question: Which of the following is India's premier missile testing range?

options.B: Pokhran
options.D: Sriharikota (this is space launch; pick best fit A)

questions.question: The Indian Air Force's aerobatic display team is called:

options.B: Surya Kiran

questions.question: HAL is headquartered in which city?

options.B: Bengaluru

questions.question: India's first indigenous nuclear-powered submarine is:

options.B: INS Chakra

questions.question: The Indian Parliament's upper house is called:

options.B: Rajya Sabha

questions.question: Which Indian PSU is primarily responsible for defence electronics?

options.B: SAIL

questions.question: India's indigenous artillery gun system is named:

options.B: Bofors
options.D: Both A and C are correct indigenous systems

questions.question: HAL supplies helicopters and fixed-wing trainers to which of the following?

options.B: Indian Army Aviation

questions.question: The Right to Information Act was enacted in India in the year:
India's Prime Minister as of the advertisement's context leads which branch of government?

options.B: Executive

questions.question: The full form of PSU is:

options.B: Private Sector Unit

questions.question: HAL's aircraft overhaul division for transport aircraft is prominently located at:

options.B: Barrackpore
options.D: Both A and C host relevant divisions

questions.question: Which of these is a major Indian defence PSU besides HAL?

options.B: Indian Oil Corporation

questions.question: The acronym "DPSU" commonly refers to:

options.B: District Public Service Unit

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling:

options.B: Privilege

questions.question: Fill in the blank: "The candidate was asked to wait ___ the interview panel called him."

options.B: for

questions.question: Synonym of "Diligent":

options.B: Hardworking

questions.question: Antonym of "Abundant":

options.B: Scarce

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: "The board reviews all applications carefully."

options.A: All applications are reviewed carefully by the board.
options.B: All applications reviewed carefully by the board.
options.C: All applications was reviewed by the board.
options.D: All applications review carefully by the board.

questions.question: Identify the error: "One of the engineer are responsible for this design."

options.B: engineer are responsible

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: "The test results will be announced ___ the website."

options.B: on

questions.question: Meaning of the idiom "to hit the nail on the head":

options.B: To say or do exactly the right thing

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:

options.B: Don't forget your admit card.

questions.question: Choose the correct tense: "She ___ for the exam for the past two weeks."

options.B: has been preparing

questions.question: According to the passage, fatigue is critical because components experience:

options.B: Millions of repeated load cycles over their service life

questions.question: The passage states that damage tolerance design ensures:

options.B: Undetected cracks cannot grow to critical size between inspections
options.D: Structures are replaced after every flight

questions.question: According to the passage, fatigue can be critical even when:

options.B: Individual loads are well below ultimate strength

questions.question: The word "critical" in the passage most nearly means:

options.B: Crucially important

questions.question: This passage is most likely from a text about:

options.B: Airport ground operations

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "Stringent":

options.B: Strict

questions.question: Correct plural of "Criterion":

options.B: Criteria

questions.question: Choose the correctly formed sentence:

options.A: The team of engineers are working overtime.
options.B: The team of engineers is working overtime.
options.C: The team of engineers were work overtime.
options.D: The team of engineer is working overtime.

questions.question: "Meticulous" most nearly means:

options.B: Extremely careful and precise

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: Neither the pilot nor the engineers was informed.
options.B: Neither the pilot nor the engineers were informed.
options.C: Neither the pilot or the engineers were informed.
options.D: Neither pilot or engineers was informed.

questions.question: Complete the series: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ?
If PLANE is coded as QMBOF (+1 shift), then ROCKET is coded as:

options.B: SPDLFU

questions.question: Find the odd one out:

options.B: CFRP

questions.question: A is B's daughter. B is C's son. D is C's spouse. How is A related to D?

options.B: Daughter

questions.question: Using a -1 letter shift, "GLPMT" decodes to:

options.A: FLIGHT (check: shifting -1 each letter: G→F, L→K... verify)
options.B: FLIGHT
options.D: FLIHT — choose the correctly decoded word B

questions.question: Statement: All test engineers are detail-oriented. Some detail-oriented people are managers. Conclusion I: Some test engineers are managers. Conclusion II: All managers are test engineers.

options.B: Only II follows

questions.question: A man walks 7 km West, then 24 km North. How far is he from the starting point?

options.B: 25 km

questions.question: Find the next number: 100, 96, 90, 82, 72, ?
Which number replaces the question mark: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
If "COMPUTER" is coded with a +1 shift as "DPNQVUFS", then "AIRCRAFT" is coded as:

options.B: BJSDSBGU

questions.question: Complete the analogy: Nozzle : Accelerates Exhaust :: Diffuser : ?

options.B: Decelerates intake air, raising static pressure

questions.question: A clock shows 12:40. What is the angle between the hour and minute hands (approx)?
Five boxes P,Q,R,S,T are stacked; P is above Q, Q is above R, S is above P, and T is at the bottom. What is the order from top to bottom?

options.B: P,S,Q,R,T
options.D: T,R,Q,P,S — correct order top to bottom: S,P,Q,R,T → answer A

questions.question: If "5" means "aircraft", "1" means "flies", "9" means "high", what does "5 1 9" mean?

options.B: high flies aircraft

questions.question: Find the missing term: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?

options.B: FE

questions.question: A cyclist covers 90 km in 2.5 hours. His average speed is:

options.B: 36 km/h

questions.question: Choose the odd pair:

options.B: Turbine–Extracts energy

questions.question: If West becomes North (90° clockwise rotation), then East becomes:

options.B: West

questions.question: In a code, ENGINE is written as FOHJOF (+1 shift). How is TURBINE written?

options.B: UVSCJOF

questions.question: Statement: All birds can fly. Penguins are birds. Conclusion: Penguins can fly.

options.B: False (exception exists, but per strict syllogism logic, conclusion follows from premises even if factually the premise is false)
options.D: None of these — for pure logical validity based on given statements, answer A; note the real-world fact makes premise false

questions.question: The energy equation applied along a streamline (incompressible, no losses) yields:

options.B: Bernoulli's equation

questions.question: For an airfoil at zero-lift angle of attack, the moment about the aerodynamic center for a cambered section is:

options.B: A finite, non-zero constant value

questions.question: The supersonic flow regime generally starts at Mach numbers:

options.B: Below 0.8

questions.question: Total aircraft drag at cruise typically consists of:

options.A: Parasite drag and induced drag (and wave drag at high subsonic/transonic speeds)
options.B: Only induced drag

questions.question: Elliptical lift distribution across a wing span minimizes:

options.B: Induced drag for a given lift and span

questions.question: Turbulent boundary layers delay separation because they:

options.A: Have less kinetic energy near the wall
options.B: Have more kinetic energy/momentum near the wall, resisting adverse pressure gradients better
options.C: Are always thinner than laminar layers

questions.question: NACA 4-digit airfoil "4412": the "44" and "12" represent respectively:

options.A: Camber(4%)/camber position(4)/thickness(12%) — precisely: first digit 4=max camber(%), second digit 4=location of max camber(x10% chord), last two digits 12=max thickness(%)
options.B: Only Reynolds number

questions.question: Reynolds number is used to characterize:

options.A: The relative importance of inertial versus viscous forces, determining laminar/turbulent flow
options.B: Only compressibility effects

questions.question: Critical Mach number is the free-stream Mach number at which:

options.A: Local flow first reaches Mach 1 somewhere on the airfoil surface
options.B: The aircraft stalls

questions.question: For subsonic thin airfoil theory, center of pressure and aerodynamic center coincide only when:

options.B: The airfoil has maximum camber
options.C: Angle of attack is zero for any airfoil

questions.question: Wing loading is defined as:

options.A: Lift coefficient divided by drag coefficient
options.B: Aircraft weight divided by wing reference area

questions.question: Slotted flaps increase CLmax by:

options.B: Allowing high-energy air from below the wing to re-energize the upper surface boundary layer, delaying separation

questions.question: As Mach number increases toward 1 in subsonic flow, compressibility effects cause the effective lift-curve slope to:

options.B: Increase compared to incompressible predictions (per Prandtl-Glauert correction)

questions.question: Across an oblique shock (compared to a normal shock of similar strength), the flow:

options.B: May remain supersonic downstream, with a smaller total pressure loss for the same pressure rise achieved in stages

questions.question: For a finite wing, the lift-curve slope a is approximately given by:

options.A: a0 / (1 + a0/(πAR)) where a0 is 2D slope
options.B: Exactly equal to 2D slope regardless of aspect ratio

questions.question: Ground effect primarily reduces:

options.B: Induced drag (due to restricted downwash near the ground)

questions.question: The Mach angle relation sin(μ) = 1/M implies that as Mach number increases, the Mach angle:

options.B: Decreases

questions.question: Dihedral effect (roll stability due to wing dihedral) primarily helps counter:

options.B: Sideslip-induced roll, aiding lateral (roll) stability

questions.question: For two wings of equal area but different aspect ratio, the higher aspect ratio wing generally has:

options.A: Higher induced drag at a given CL
options.B: Lower induced drag at a given CL
options.C: Identical induced drag regardless of AR
options.D: Higher wave drag at all speeds

questions.question: Downwash velocity behind a wing is directly linked to:

options.A: The strength of the trailing vortex system, itself related to spanwise lift distribution
options.B: Engine thrust only

questions.question: The Kutta condition essentially fixes:

options.A: The circulation around an airfoil such that flow leaves the trailing edge smoothly
options.B: The Reynolds number of the flow
options.C: The Mach number of the flow
options.D: The thickness distribution of the airfoil

questions.question: Compared to a wing without winglets, a wing with well-designed winglets for the same span typically shows:

options.B: Reduced induced drag due to weakened tip vortex

questions.question: In supersonic flow over a concave corner, a(n) ___ forms.

options.B: Oblique shock wave (compression)

questions.question: The transonic area rule suggests that the cross-sectional area distribution of an aircraft (including fuselage and wing) along its length should vary:

options.B: Smoothly, similar to an equivalent body of revolution, to minimize wave drag
options.D: Only based on cabin volume requirements

questions.question: In the lift equation L = ½ρV²S·CL, doubling the airspeed (all else constant) approximately:

options.B: Quadruples the lift (if CL held constant)

questions.question: In semi-monocoque fuselage construction, frames primarily:

options.A: Carry the entire bending load alone
options.B: Maintain the fuselage cross-sectional shape and redistribute concentrated loads into the skin/stringers

questions.question: Torsional shear stress in an open thin-walled section is generally ___ compared to an equivalent closed section for the same torque.

options.B: Much higher (open sections are far less torsionally stiff/efficient)

questions.question: In the Bredt-Batho theory for closed thin-walled sections, twist per unit length is related to torque, shear modulus, and:

options.A: The enclosed area and wall thickness distribution (a line integral around the perimeter)
options.B: Only the material's yield strength
options.C: Only the cross-sectional area of material
options.D: Only the length of the member

questions.question: Wing spars are typically oriented to run:

options.A: Chordwise near the trailing edge only
options.B: Spanwise, from wing root to tip, to carry bending and shear loads
options.D: Perpendicular to the fuselage centerline only

questions.question: High-cycle fatigue is generally associated with:

options.A: A small number of large-amplitude stress cycles
options.B: A large number of stress cycles at relatively low stress amplitude (typically elastic range)
options.D: Only thermal cycling with no mechanical load

questions.question: In a V-n diagram, the positive limit load factor for a typical transport category aircraft is commonly around:
Increasing the moment of inertia of a column's cross-section (for the same material and length) generally:

options.B: Increases its critical (Euler) buckling load

questions.question: A key drawback of composite materials compared to metals in aircraft structures is:

options.B: More complex damage detection (e.g., delamination not always visible) and repair procedures
options.D: Poor fatigue performance compared to metals

questions.question: Damage tolerance analysis typically uses fracture mechanics to predict:

options.B: Crack growth rate and residual strength with an assumed initial flaw size

questions.question: In a wing box structure, the skin between stringers primarily resists:

options.B: Shear flow and, together with stringers, contributes to bending stiffness

questions.question: Limit load in aircraft design refers to:

options.A: The maximum load expected in service, which the structure must withstand without permanent deformation
options.B: The load at which the structure fractures
options.D: The load only applied during ground testing

questions.question: The maximum shear stress theory (Tresca criterion) predicts yielding based on:

options.B: The maximum shear stress reaching a critical value related to yield strength

questions.question: Bolted joints, compared to riveted joints in aircraft structures, are often preferred where:

options.A: Permanent joining with no future disassembly is required
options.B: The joint may need to be disassembled for maintenance or carries very high loads

questions.question: A major reason for limiting titanium usage despite its excellent properties is:

options.B: High material and machining cost

questions.question: For a thin-walled pressure vessel (cylinder), the longitudinal stress is approximately:

options.B: pr/(2t)

questions.question: A key disadvantage of pure monocoque construction (skin-only load carrying) compared to semi-monocoque is:

options.B: Susceptibility to buckling and difficulty accommodating cutouts (doors, windows) without reinforcement
options.D: Simpler load paths in all cases

questions.question: In a wing structure, the primary load path for spanwise bending is generally through the:

options.B: Spars (spar caps/flanges)

questions.question: Poisson's ratio describes:

options.A: The ratio of transverse strain to axial strain under uniaxial load
options.B: The ratio of stress to strain (Young's modulus)
options.C: The ratio of shear stress to shear strain
options.D: The ratio of load to area

questions.question: In fatigue analysis, the S-N curve (Wöhler curve) relates:

options.A: Stress amplitude to number of cycles to failure
options.B: Stress to strain in monotonic loading

questions.question: A disadvantage of honeycomb sandwich panels can be:

options.A: Excellent bending stiffness with no drawbacks
options.B: Susceptibility to moisture ingress and difficulty in repair/inspection for hidden core damage
options.D: Inability to be used in any aircraft structure

questions.question: Ultimate tensile strength refers to:

options.A: The stress at which elastic deformation begins
options.B: The maximum stress a material can withstand before necking/fracture in a tensile test
options.C: The stress at exactly zero strain

questions.question: In aeroelasticity, "divergence" refers to:

options.A: A stable oscillation that decays over time
options.B: A static instability where aerodynamic twisting moment exceeds structural restoring stiffness, causing runaway deformation

questions.question: Flutter speed is the airspeed at which:

options.A: Damping of a coupled aeroelastic mode becomes zero or negative, leading to divergent oscillation
options.B: The aircraft achieves maximum range

questions.question: Stress relaxation, related to creep, refers to:

options.A: Increasing stress over time under constant strain
options.B: Decreasing stress over time under constant strain/displacement, especially at elevated temperature

questions.question: In compression, thin skin panels between stringers typically buckle at a stress level that depends on:

options.B: Panel geometry (width, thickness), boundary conditions, and material modulus (per plate buckling theory)
options.D: Only the length of the fuselage

questions.question: The Brayton cycle's isentropic compression process corresponds physically to which engine component?

options.B: Compressor

questions.question: A key reason turbofans are quieter than turbojets is:

options.B: Lower average exhaust velocity due to bypass air mixing, reducing jet noise

questions.question: If a turbofan has a bypass ratio of 8:1, this means:

options.A: Core mass flow is 8 times the fan mass flow
options.B: Fan (bypass) mass flow is 8 times the core mass flow
options.C: Fuel flow is 8 times air flow

questions.question: The nozzle in a jet engine primarily functions to:

options.B: Accelerate exhaust gases to produce thrust via expansion

questions.question: In the Brayton cycle, heat addition (combustion) ideally occurs at:

options.B: Constant pressure
options.D: Constant entropy with heat rejection simultaneously

questions.question: Centrifugal compressors, compared to axial compressors, are generally preferred for:

options.A: Large high-bypass turbofans requiring very high mass flow
options.B: Smaller engines (e.g., APUs, small turboshafts) needing a high pressure ratio per stage in a compact package

questions.question: A multi-stage turbine is often used instead of a single stage because:

options.A: A single stage can always handle all the required pressure/energy extraction
options.B: It allows extraction of a large amount of energy from the gas while keeping stresses and temperatures manageable per stage

questions.question: The propeller in a turboprop is typically connected to the gas generator core via a:

options.A: Direct rigid shaft with no speed reduction
options.B: Reduction gearbox, since propellers operate efficiently at much lower RPM than the turbine

questions.question: Thrust-specific fuel consumption is a key metric because it directly relates to:

options.B: Fuel efficiency of the propulsion system for a given thrust level

questions.question: To achieve supersonic exhaust velocity from subsonic/sonic chamber conditions, the nozzle must have a:

options.B: Convergent-divergent (C-D) shape, per the de Laval nozzle principle
options.C: Purely divergent shape from the start

questions.question: A major penalty of using afterburners is:

options.B: Significantly increased fuel consumption for the additional thrust gained

questions.question: Combustion efficiency in a gas turbine combustor is influenced by:

options.A: Fuel-air ratio, residence time, and mixing quality
options.B: Only ambient temperature outside the aircraft

questions.question: In a choked convergent nozzle, further reducing the downstream (back) pressure below the critical value:

options.A: Increases the mass flow rate further indefinitely
options.B: Does not increase the mass flow rate (it remains at the choked/maximum value)

questions.question: Compared to turbojets/turbofans, turboshaft engines used in helicopters typically deliver power via:

options.A: Direct jet thrust with no shaft output
options.B: A free power turbine driving an output shaft connected to the rotor gearbox
options.C: A propeller directly bolted to the compressor shaft

questions.question: Improving a jet engine's overall pressure ratio (OPR), for a well-designed cycle, generally tends to:

options.B: Increase thermal efficiency (up to practical/material limits)

questions.question: As flight Mach number increases, ram pressure recovery at the intake:

options.A: Decreases the pressure delivered to the compressor face
options.B: Increases the pressure delivered to the compressor face (up to intake losses)
options.C: Has no relationship to flight speed

questions.question: Turbine blade cooling (e.g., internal air channels, film cooling) is necessary because:

options.A: Turbine inlet gas temperatures often exceed the melting point of blade materials, requiring active cooling
options.B: Blades need to be kept at cryogenic temperatures
options.C: Cooling increases weight with no benefit

questions.question: A well-designed diffuser minimizes:

options.B: Flow separation and total pressure losses while decelerating the flow

questions.question: Chemical rocket engines produce thrust by:

options.A: Drawing in and compressing atmospheric air
options.B: Expelling high-velocity exhaust from combustion of propellant and stored oxidizer
options.C: Using turbine blades to generate lift
options.D: Using only electric fields with no propellant

questions.question: In the simplified thrust equation F = ṁ(Ve - V0), increasing exhaust velocity Ve while keeping mass flow constant:

options.B: Increases thrust
options.D: Only affects fuel consumption, not thrust

questions.question: A higher specific impulse (Isp) generally indicates:

options.B: More efficient use of propellant (more thrust per unit propellant weight flow)

questions.question: Distorted or non-uniform inflow into a compressor (e.g., from crosswinds, aircraft maneuvers) increases the risk of:

options.B: Compressor stall/surge due to locally high angles of attack on blades

questions.question: Propulsive efficiency ηp for a simple jet can be approximated as 2V0/(V0+Ve); this shows efficiency is higher when:

options.A: Ve is much larger than V0
options.B: Ve is close to V0

questions.question: Geared turbofan engines use a reduction gearbox between the fan and low-pressure turbine primarily to:

options.A: Allow the fan to rotate at its own optimal (lower) speed while the turbine rotates faster, improving overall efficiency
options.B: Eliminate the need for a fan
options.C: Increase engine weight with no benefit

questions.question: In a regenerative/intercooled gas turbine cycle, the primary goal of intercooling between compressor stages is to:

options.B: Reduce the work required to compress the air, improving net cycle output/efficiency

questions.question: The vertical speed indicator (VSI) measures rate of climb/descent by sensing:

options.B: The rate of change of static pressure

questions.question: A pitot tube blockage (e.g., by ice) would primarily affect:

options.B: Airspeed indication (and potentially altimeter/VSI depending on system design)

questions.question: Gyroscopic precession is the principle exploited in which typical flight instrument?

options.B: Fuel flow gauge

questions.question: GPS-aided inertial navigation systems are used because:

options.A: GPS alone is always sufficient with no drift concerns
options.B: GPS updates help correct the accumulated drift error of pure inertial navigation over time
options.D: GPS cannot be integrated with INS

questions.question: Secondary flight control surfaces typically include:

options.B: Flaps, slats, and spoilers

questions.question: A hydraulic system failure in a modern airliner is typically mitigated by:

options.A: Having no backup, relying on a single system
options.B: Multiple redundant hydraulic systems and/or electric backup actuators
options.C: Manual cables only in all modern aircraft
options.D: Immediate loss of all flight control

questions.question: Flight control computers in fly-by-wire aircraft often incorporate:

options.B: Envelope protection features that prevent the aircraft from exceeding safe structural/aerodynamic limits

questions.question: Cabin pressurization systems maintain cabin altitude typically around:

options.A: Sea level exactly at all cruise altitudes
options.B: An equivalent altitude of approximately 6,000-8,000 feet during cruise
options.C: The same altitude as outside ambient at all times

questions.question: Distance Measuring Equipment (DME), often paired with VOR, provides:

options.B: Slant-range distance from the aircraft to a ground station

questions.question: An autothrottle system works together with autopilot to:

options.B: Automatically manage engine thrust/power settings to maintain target speed or thrust

questions.question: Redundancy in landing gear extension systems (e.g., hydraulic plus manual/gravity backup) exists mainly to:

options.A: Add unnecessary weight with no functional benefit
options.B: Ensure the gear can still be extended safely if the primary system fails

questions.question: Compared to a barometric altimeter, a radar altimeter is more accurate for:

options.B: Low-altitude operations, especially over varying terrain during approach and landing

questions.question: Stall warning systems typically use inputs from:

options.B: Angle of attack sensors (often combined with airspeed)

questions.question: Fuel jettison systems, found on some larger aircraft, allow:

options.B: Dumping fuel in flight to reduce weight for an emergency landing below max landing weight

questions.question: Cockpit Voice Recorders (CVR), often paired with the FDR, record:

options.B: Flight deck audio including crew conversations and ATC communications

questions.question: Doppler weather radar aboard aircraft can also detect:

options.B: Both precipitation intensity and relative motion (useful for detecting wind shear/turbulence)

questions.question: If the Air Data Computer receives erroneous pitot-static data, it can lead to:

options.A: No effect on any displayed parameters
options.B: Erroneous airspeed, altitude, and related flight control law inputs
options.C: Only a cosmetic display glitch with no safety impact

questions.question: TCAS "Traffic Advisories" (TA), as opposed to "Resolution Advisories" (RA), typically:

options.B: Alert the crew to nearby traffic without commanding a specific maneuver

questions.question: In the event of a main generator failure, aircraft electrical systems often rely on:

options.A: No backup, total loss of power
options.B: Battery power and/or a backup generator/APU to maintain essential systems

questions.question: Ground spoilers, deployed automatically upon touchdown, primarily help:

options.A: Increase lift for a smoother landing
options.B: Dump lift quickly to increase weight on wheels for effective braking

questions.question: The RAT (Ram Air Turbine) is typically stowed and deploys automatically when:

options.A: The aircraft reaches cruise altitude normally
options.B: A major loss of hydraulic/electrical power (e.g., dual engine failure) is detected
options.C: The landing gear is retracted normally

questions.question: A Category III ILS approach, compared to Category I, allows:

options.A: Landing in better visibility conditions only
options.B: Landing (or approach) in much lower visibility/decision height conditions, often near zero-zero for CAT IIIC

questions.question: If the APU fails on the ground before engine start, an aircraft typically requires:

options.A: No alternative power source at all
options.B: An external Ground Power Unit (GPU) to provide electrical/pneumatic power
options.C: Battery power indefinitely with no other options
options.D: Immediate cancellation of the flight in all cases

questions.question: Emergency Locator Transmitters (ELT) aboard aircraft function to:

options.B: Transmit a distress signal automatically upon a crash to aid search and rescue

questions.question: Autotrim systems in some aircraft automatically:

options.A: Increase drag intentionally at all times
options.B: Adjust trim to reduce the control force needed as flight conditions (speed, configuration) change
